Edition year/date of the cdc_child schedule is not stated in this section; version and effective_date set to 'unstated' for human completion.
Minimum ages (6 weeks for PCV15/PCV20; 2 years for PPSV23) and product choice (PCV15 vs PCV20 vs PPSV23) are not represented.

The routine rule requires 4 PCV doses; children who started late and completed an age-appropriate catch-up series with fewer doses (per Table 2) are complete per the text's footnote definition but would be flagged as not meeting the rule. Human review should consider this.

Catch-up for healthy children ages 2-4 years with an incomplete PCV series (1 dose PCV) not encoded: 'incomplete' depends on age-appropriate catch-up series logic in Table 2, and 'healthy' requires absence of all risk conditions.
Note that PCV20 is not indicated for children without risk conditions who received 4 doses of PCV13/PCV15 or another complete age-appropriate series is a 'not indicated' statement; not a rule.

Special situations for children 2-5 and 6-18 years with CSF leak, chronic heart/kidney (excluding maintenance dialysis and nephrotic syndrome)/liver/lung disease (incl. moderate or severe persistent asthma), cochlear implant, or diabetes: dose counts depend on prior doses (3 vs fewer than 3), prior product (PCV13/PCV15/PCV20/PPSV23), age at prior doses, and minimum intervals (at least 8 weeks); not encoded.

Special situations for children on maintenance dialysis or with immunocompromising conditions (nephrotic syndrome, asplenia/splenic dysfunction, immunodeficiencies, immunosuppressive therapy, malignancies, transplant, HIV infection, sickle cell disease/hemoglobinopathies): same prior-dose-dependent logic plus PCV20 or dose 2 PPSV23 at least 5 years after dose 1 PPSV23; not encoded. Concepts would include chronic_kidney_disease, immunocompromised, asplenia, hiv_infection, csf_leak, cochlear_implant, diabetes, ppsv23_vaccine; no concept exists for maintenance dialysis, nephrotic syndrome, or PCV product type (PCV13/PCV15/PCV20 distinction).
Sequencing rule: when both PCV15 and PPSV23 are indicated give all PCV15 doses first and do not give PCV15 and PPSV23 at the same visit; scheduling logic not encoded.
Pregnancy: no recommendation for PCV or PPSV23 due to limited data; not a rule.
Mobile app reference and footnote definition of incomplete series (Table 2 of ACIP recommendations) are external references not represented.
